acceptance_criteria: `PointRef::ArcStart(id)` and `PointRef::ArcEnd(id)` (or equivalent) name an arc's start and end points. Using them on a non-arc returns `SketchError::KindMismatch`.

Every constraint that takes a `PointRef` accepts them: coincident, horizontal/vertical points, fixed, distance, midpoint (as the point), symmetric. Each residual has an analytic Jacobian that includes the arc's center, radius and angle.

Test: a slot (2 lines, 2 arcs, radius 5, centers 30 apart) drawn roughly, with arc angles off by 10° or more, is closed by 4 coincident constraints. After solving, every arc end coincides with its line end within 1e-8, and `profiles` returns 1 region with area 300 + 25π ± 1e-6.
Test: that slot with tangent ×4, equal, radius, horizontal, fixed center and center distance 30 is `FullyConstrained` (dof 0).
DOF analysis counts the new rows correctly (coincident with an arc end adds 2 equations).
Arc sweep stays in (0, 2π) after solving, or the behavior when an arc would flip is documented and tested.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M2-04a: Constraints can name an arc's start and end points, so arcs join lines (slots, rounded corners)
